dct_description_sm: Seafood is an important source of nutrients for many populations worldwide. Unfortunately the contamination of seafood with methylmercury (MeHg) has raised health concerns, particularly for developing infants. The modification of MeHg toxicity by nutrients, including antioxidants, has been reported in both epidemiological and animal exposure studies. The objectives of this laboratory-based study are (1) to better characterize and evaluate the robustness of biomarkers of MeHg exposure/effects at low doses and for different co-exposure scenarios, (2) better understand the molecular mechanisms underlying contaminant-nutrient interactions, and (3) assess nutritional approaches to mitigate methylmercury neurotoxicity, using Labrador tea, a locally available and culturally relevant concoction with interesting antioxidant properties (Dufour et al., 2006). A better understanding of contaminant-nutrient interactions will lead to better risk assessment and strategies to minimize the impact of environmental contaminants on the health of Canadian Arctic populations.
dct_subject_sm: Health sciences and contaminants -> Traditional food
dct_title_s: Modulation of the effects of methylmercury on rat neurodevelopment by co-exposure with Labrador Tea
